title: Rejoining Ory in the 1920s and the 1922 Sunshine records
summary: Garland names the Ory band (Wilson, Darensbourg, Carey, Hall, Scott) which made the first records by Black musicians in Los Angeles, c. 1922, for Sunshine.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Oh, you bet. Good ears, too. I know your playing. I know your playing. That's exciting. So after Black and Tan what did you do? Did you go back to Orrie?
I went back to Ory, yeah.
Now, who was in the Ory band at this time?
When I went back to Ory?
All right. I'll tell you who was back there. I'll start with Buster Wilson on the piano. Joe Dorersbourg on clarinet. Papa Mutt [Carey] on the trumpet. Ram Hall on the drums. Bud Scott on the -
And Orrie on the trombone. And Tudi Tootie Garland on the bass.
Oh, it was a wonderful band. Were you in that movie? Was there a movie that this band was in? Did this band ever get in a movie or make records?
Yeah. We made the first records black boys made (Unintelligible) -- in Los Angeles.
In 1922 I think it was. For Sunshine Records.
Okay. Right. That's what I remember. That's a wonderful band. That's a wonderful band.
